1. The Software

Chennai BnB PMS is a Property Management System for a small 8-room serviced-apartment property. It lets front-desk staff manage rooms, guests and the complete booking lifecycle, and exposes the same data through a REST API.

Technology stack

LayerTechnology
BackendPython 3 / Flask (server-rendered Jinja2 templates + REST API)
DatabaseMySQL 8.0 via mysql-connector-python
FrontendHTML5 + CSS (Jinja2 templates), vanilla JavaScript
AuthFlask server-side sessions, role-based access control
Test automationpytest + requests (API/DB), Playwright (browser UI)

Core features

  • Authentication & roles - three roles (manager, reception, auditor) with per-endpoint authorisation.
  • Dashboard - live occupancy rate, available/occupied counts, today's check-ins and check-outs.
  • Room management - list all rooms, edit price and status (available / occupied / maintenance).
  • Guest management - guest records created automatically from bookings, with contact details and ID proof.
  • Booking lifecycle - create a booking, check in, check out or cancel, with automatic room-status cascade.
  • Availability engine - date-range overlap detection prevents double-booking; maintenance rooms are excluded.
  • REST API - 11 JSON endpoints covering rooms, bookings, guests, availability and occupancy reporting.
  • Security hardening - CSP, X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and no-store headers on every response.

User roles

RoleLoginPermissions
Managermanager / manager123Full access including booking mutation
Receptionreception / reception123Bookings, guests, rooms, availability
Auditorauditor / auditor123Read-only reporting; blocked from mutating bookings

2. Architecture & Data Model

The application is a single Flask service. Browser requests are served as Jinja2-rendered HTML; the same Database layer also backs the JSON API, so the UI and the API always read and write identical records in MySQL.

Request flow: Browser / API client → Flask route (auth decorator) → validation → Database class → MySQL → JSON or rendered template.

Database schema

TableKey columnsNotes
roomsroom_id, room_number (UNIQUE), room_type, base_price, status, floor, current_guest_id, current_booking_id8 seeded rooms; status is an ENUM
guestsguest_id, name, email, phone, id_proof, created_atCreated automatically when a booking is made
bookingsbooking_id, room_id (FK), guest_id (FK), check_in, check_out, total_price, status, checked_in_at, checked_out_atFKs cascade on delete; status is an ENUM

Booking lifecycle

confirmed → checked_in → checked_out, with cancelled reachable from any active state. Creating a booking marks the room occupied; checking out or cancelling returns it to available - but only when no other active booking still holds that room.

REST API endpoints

MethodEndpointAuth
GET/api/hotel-infonone
GET/api/roomsnone
GET, PUT/api/rooms/<id>none
GET/api/rooms/<id>/guestany role
GET/api/rooms/availableany role

GET, PUT, DELETE/api/bookings/<id>manager, reception
GET/api/guestsany role
GET/api/guests/<id>any role
GET/api/guests/checked-inany role

3. Test Strategy & Tooling

30 automated test cases were written and are organised into the three categories required by the assignment. Tests run at two layers so the same system is verified from the outside (browser) and at the contract level (HTTP + SQL).

LayerToolingWhat it covers
UIPlaywright (Chromium)Real browser journeys; every test captures a screenshot
APIpytest + requestsStatus codes, JSON payloads, validation and RBAC
Databasemysql-connectorDirect SQL assertions that data really persisted

Test isolation

Every test runs against a database reset to the identical 8-room seed state, so results are deterministic and the suite can be re-run live, repeatedly, without drift. The Flask server is started automatically by the test session.

6. Defects Found (open)

These defects remain in the build and are what the failing tests detect.

RefTestDefect
D1E2E-08Lockout helpers _is_login_locked() / _record_failed_login() are defined in app.py but never called by the /login route, so no lockout ever triggers.
D3INT-08PUT /api/rooms/<id> mutates a throwaway dictionary and never writes to MySQL, yet still reports Room updated successfully.
D4INT-09/api/bookings carries no authentication decorator, so an anonymous caller can create bookings freely.
D6BND-12The API only checks that required keys exist, not that they hold a value, so a blank guest name is accepted and a booking is created.
D7BND-05The availability check parses the dates before the guarded try/except block, so a malformed date raises an uncaught ValueError and leaks an HTTP 500 instead of a clean 400.
D8BND-11The guest INSERT is unguarded, so MySQL strict mode raises Data too long and the request returns HTTP 500 rather than a validation error.

7. Defects Found & Fixed

These were discovered while building the suite and have been repaired. Their tests now pass, which is the evidence that the fix works.

D2 — /new-booking form validation
The booking form had no validation at all: a malformed date crashed with a 500 and reversed dates created a booking with a negative total. It now validates required fields, date format, date ordering and room availability.
Verified by: BND-13, E2E-03, E2E-04, INT-05
D5 — /rooms/edit persistence & validation
The room edit form mutated a throwaway dictionary and saved nothing, and accepted any price. It now writes through to MySQL and rejects a price of zero or less.
Verified by: E2E-05
D9 — Database connection leak on error
create_guest() and create_booking() never closed their connection when an INSERT failed, leaving an open transaction holding table locks. Both now release the connection in a finally block.
Verified by: Prevented the suite from hanging on BND-11

8. How to Run the Demo

#StepCommand
1Ensure MySQL is running and the schema is loadedmysql -u root -p < schema.sql
2Run the whole suite (starts the app automatically)python -m pytest -v
3Run one category onlypython -m pytest tests/test_category2_boundary.py -v
4Run only the browser tests (add --headed to watch)python -m pytest tests/test_category1_e2e_ui.py --headed
5Regenerate the HTML reportpython -m pytest --html=test_evidence/report.html --self-contained-html
6Rebuild this document (after a run)python tools/capture_evidence.py
python tools/render_api_cards.py
python tools/build_demo_document.py
Live demo tip: run step 4 with --headed --slowmo 600 to show Chromium driving the application in real time - filling the booking form, checking a guest in and checking them out - then run step 2 to show the full suite and the defects it catches.
